page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, providing 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes 237 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard operations. The server achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 1864.0 and a multi-core score of 5890.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 462.09 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 96.75 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable strength, placing in the top 25% with 14.27 GB/sec. However, cryptographic performance is weak, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 10% at 751.42. Large-model LLM inference is also limited, yielding 6.18 tokens/sec for a 7B model.

The r8gd.xlarge offers a balanced resource density for memory-bound workloads requiring local scratch space, delivering high memory capacity per core alongside integrated NVMe storage. This hardware profile is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and memory-intensive data processing tasks that do not rely heavily on x86-specific instruction sets or intensive cryptographic acceleration.
